newsitem.title: USA: Clinton - Israel, Palestians agree on Hebron talks.
newsitem.headline: Clinton - Israel, Palestians agree on Hebron talks.

text.p: President Bill Clinton announced on Wednesday that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat have agreed to resume immediate peace talks with priority on discussion of an Israeli pullback from the West Bank city of Hebron.

"They are ready to renew and intensify negotiations on implementing the interim (Israeli-Palestinian peace) agreement with Hebron as the first priority," Clinton said in issuing a "summary statement" on two days of Middle East crisis talks in Washington.

"They are committed to engaging immediately in talks and to achieving tangible progress," he said. "To assist them in this effort I am sending Dennis Ross, our special Middle East coordinator, to the region now."

"The very first meeting will take place on Sunday morning in Erez," on the Israeli-Gaza border, he said at a joint appearance in the White House East Room with Arafat, Netanyahu and Jordan's King Hussein.

Clinton said these developments indicated that considerable success had been achieved at the summit, which he called in hopes of saving Middle East peace negotiations from collapse following renewed violence in the West Bank and Gaza last week. He said he wanted all sides to get this message from the meeting: "I'm convinced that this process and these parties are in better shape than they were two days ago and please, please give us a chance to make this thing work."
